newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to scrap law hindering media freedom.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to scrap law hindering media freedom.

text.p: The Sri Lankan government plans to scrap a 19-year-old law which makes journalists answerable to parliament in cases where legislators were alleged to have been discredited by the media.

Media Minister Mangala Samaraweera said on Thursday the government would soon introduce a motion to repeal the Parliamentary Privileges Special Provisions Act of 1978, which was introduced by the former United National Party (UNP) government.

"It gave parliament the right to fine and also imprison journalists and editors. We feel this is a gross violation of the freedom of media and one which goes against parliamentary democracy," Samaraweera told a news conference.
The act was introduced by the then government after a photograph published in a state-owned newspaper was claimed by a senior UNP legislator to have harmed his reputation, Samaraweera said.
It has been used at least twice against the media.
Lawmakers' privileges include parliament's ability to interrogate and pass judgement on those whose words or actions are alleged to have damaged the credibility and reputation of legislators.
The UNP's 17-year rule was ended in 1994 by the People's Alliance headed by President Chandrika Kumaratunga.
